title: Teapot: Efficiently Uncovering Spectre Gadgets in COTS Binaries
problem: Spectre vulnerabilities persist in deployed binaries; existing gadget detection either requires source code or suffers runtime overhead and limited detection. Binary-only analysis has been impractical.
motivation: Most deployed software exists as binaries; practical Spectre gadget detection in COTS binaries enables vulnerability assessment without source access.
method: Teapot rewrites compiled binaries without source code to run two parallel execution paths: one normal, one simulating speculative execution (the CPU's process of guessing what code to run ahead of time). This technique, Speculation Shadows, tracks whether timing differences in speculative paths could leak secrets. Runtime integrity checks flag exploitable patterns, and automated testing (fuzzing) confirms which vulnerabilities actually work.
key_novelty: Speculation Shadows: a technique that instruments compiled binaries to run normal and speculative execution paths in parallel, enabling detection of exploitable Spectre gadgets.
contributions: First Spectre gadget scanner for COTS binaries with performance comparable to compiler-based tools
20x+ performance improvement over prior binary-based approaches
limitations: Not compared directly to compiler-based tools; generalization to other microarchitectural attacks not discussed.
primary_theme: efficient Spectre gadget detection in COTS binaries
